title: Assembly and purification of AvrSr35-induced Sr35 resistosome and determination of its structure by cryo-EM
protocol: Obtain plasmid carrying the full-length coding sequence of wild-type AvrSr35.
Design primers to remove sequence encoding 1–26 amino acids from the full-length coding sequence of AvrSr35 by PCR, thus generating the AvrSr35ΔSP construct.
Perform PCR with the pET28a-AvrSr35 vector as a template to generate the AvrSr35ΔSP construct.
Run a 1% agarose gel at 120 V to verify the size and purity of PCR products.
Excise the target PCR product from the gel.
Recover the excised PCR product using the OMEGA Gel Extraction Kit or another similar kit.
Quantify the recovered PCR-amplified AvrSr35ΔSP insert by Nanodrop.
Treat the PCR-amplified AvrSr35ΔSP insert with T4 DNA polymerase.
Incubate the reaction at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Incubate the reaction system at 75°C for 20 min to eliminate T4 DNA polymerase activity.
Linearize the pMCSG7 vector using SspI restriction endonuclease.
Prepare the reaction system according to the Vector linearization with SspI table.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 2 h.
Treat the linearized pMCSG7 vector with T4 DNA polymerase.
Mix the PCR-amplified AvrSr35ΔSP insert and the pMCSG7 vector as described in Ligation-independent cloning (LIC) reaction table.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Transform the ligation product pMCSG7-AvrSr35ΔSP into DH5α competent cells.
Plate the transformants onto LB agar plates containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 12–15 h.
Inoculate a single large bacterial colony into 5 mL of LB medium supplemented with 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Culture the inoculated medium at 37°C and 220 rpm for 12 h.
Extract and purify plasmid DNA using the Omega Plasmid Mini Kit or similar plasmid extraction kit.
Sequence the recombinant plasmid to confirm that the sequence of the pMCSG7-AvrSr35ΔSP is correct.
Transform the pMCSG7-AvrSr35ΔSP plasmid into the E. coli Rosetta (DE3) protein expression strain.
Plate the transformants onto LB agar plates containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin and 50 μg/mL chloramphenicol.
Pick a single, large colony with a sterile pipette tip and use it to inoculate 100 mL of liquid LB medium supplemented with 100 μg/mL ampicillin and 50 μg/mL chloramphenicol.
Culture the inoculated medium at 37°C and 220 rpm for 12 hours.
Expand the bacterial culture in 1 L of LB medium supplemented with ampicillin and chloramphenicol.
Dilute the starter culture at a ratio of 1:100 into the supplemented LB medium.
Culture the bacteria at 37°C and 220 rpm until the OD600 value reaches 0.6–0.8.
Add 300 μL of 1 M IPTG to each flask with bacterial culture, final concentration is 0.3 mM.
Express the protein at 18°C and 220 rpm for 12-15 hours.
Pellet the bacteria by centrifuging the culture at 3,100 × g and 4°C for 15 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and collect the pelleted bacteria.
Store the bacterial pellets at -20°C to -80°C if not proceeding immediately to the next step.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in pre-chilled Lysis buffer by vortexing or rocking until completely resuspended.
Disrupt the bacteria using a French press cooled to 4°C, operating at 800 bar pressure.
Alternatively, disrupt cells by sonication instead of using a French press.
Centrifuge the lysate at 10,540 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C to separate supernatant from cell debris and unbroken cells.
Equilibrate the Ni-NTA affinity column with 5 column volumes of Lysis buffer 1.
Load the supernatant onto the equilibrated Ni-NTA affinity column.
Pass the supernatant through the column at a flow rate of approximately 0.8 mL/min to ensure efficient binding of the target protein.
Wash the Ni-NTA beads with 5 column volumes of Lysis buffer 1.
Elute the bound proteins using Lysis buffer 1 containing 20 mM imidazole, followed by Lysis buffer 1 containing 200 mM imidazole.
Collect the eluate in separate tubes.
Monitor protein presence in the eluate with Bradford reagent; continue elution until no protein is detected.
Combine collected eluates and mix with protein loading buffer.
Perform SDS-PAGE gel analysis to assess purity of AvrSr35ΔSP.
Measure absorbance at 280 nm for purified proteins.
Determine A260/A280 ratio via Nanodrop; the ideal range should be between 0.5 and 0.7.
Pool the selected protein samples using a centrifugal filter with molecular weight cut-off (MWCO) value of 50 kDa.
Replace the buffer system into Buffer A (25 mM MES (pH 6.0), 100 mM NaCl, 2 mM DTT).
Concentrate and adjust the sample volume to 15 mL.
Mount the SP FF column onto a chromatography system, such as the ÄKTA pure, at 4°C.
Wash the SP FF column using at least five column volumes of Buffer B (25 mM MES (pH 6.0), 1 M NaCl, 2 mM DTT) at a flow rate of 2 mL/min.
Equilibrate the column with five column volumes of Buffer A at a flow rate of 2 mL/min.
Load the protein sample onto the SP FF cation exchange chromatography ion column at 4°C and at a flow rate of 1 mL/min using a peristaltic pump.
Elute the target protein using a NaCl gradient between Buffer A and Buffer B at a flow rate of 1 mL/min, increasing from 0% to 60% over 20 min.
Collect fractions containing protein peaks during elution.
Run SDS-PAGE analysis on collected fractions.
Select fractions corresponding to purified AvrSr35ΔSP for further purification.
Pool the purified AvrSr35ΔSP using a centrifugal filter (MWCO = 50 kDa).
Replace the buffer system into SEC buffer 1 (25 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 150 mM NaCl, 2 mM DTT).
Concentrate the sample after replacing the buffer system.
Quantify the concentration of AvrSr35ΔSP using a spectrophotometer.
Aliquot the sample appropriately in sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes to ensure an absorbance at 280 nm (A280) does not exceed 1000 absorption units.
Centrifuge the concentrated AvrSr35ΔSP sample at 7,440 × g at 4°C for 15 minutes before injection.
Inject the prepared AvrSr35ΔSP sample via the sample loop into a Superdex 200 (10/300 GL) SEC column that is equilibrated with SEC buffer 1.
Perform purification at a flow rate of 0.5–0.8 mL/min.
Collect fractions containing protein peaks and run SDS-PAGE analysis.
Pool and concentrate the collected fractions using a centrifugal filter (MWCO = 50 kDa).
Store the purified AvrSr35ΔSP at −80°C for further use.
Retrieve full-length coding sequence of Sr35 from NCBI database (GenBank: MT165900.1).
Design primers containing BamHI and XhoI recognition sites for PCR amplification of full-length Sr35 gene.
Perform PCR amplification using the designed primers to obtain full-length Sr35 gene product.
Run 1% agarose gel electrophoresis with the PCR products.
Excise the PCR-amplified insert band from the gel (2,757 bp).
Recover the excised PCR-amplified insert using an OMEGA Gel Extraction Kit or similar kit.
Quantify the concentration of recovered PCR-amplified insert.
Double-digest the PCR-amplified insert and SUMO-pFastBac1 vector using BamHI and XhoI restriction enzymes.
Incubate the double-digested products at 37°C for 2 h.
Run a 1% agarose gel electrophoresis to separate the digested bands.
Excise the digested PCR-amplified insert (919 bp) and SUMO-pFastBac1 (∼5,000 bp) vector bands from the gel.
Recover the excised DNA bands using an OMEGA Gel Extraction Kit or similar kit.
Quantify the concentration of recovered digestion products.
Mix the recovered PCR-amplified insert and SUMO-pFastBac1 vector at a molar ratio of 3:1.
Incubate the mixture with T4 DNA ligase at 37°C for 4 h.
Transform the ligation product into DH5α competent cells.
Plate the transformants onto LB agar plates containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 12–15 h.
Use a single large bacterial colony to inoculate 10 mL of LB medium supplemented with 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Culture the bacteria at 37°C and 220 rpm for 12 h.
Extract and purify plasmid DNA using an Omega Plasmid Mini Kit or similar kit.
Sequence the recombinant plasmid to confirm the sequence of pFastBac1-Sr35.
Place vials with 100 μL of DH10Bac competent cells on ice until thawed.
Mix 100 ng of Sumo-pFastBac1-Sr35 with the thawed DH10Bac competent cells using a sterile pipette tip.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock the cells in a 42°C water bath for 45 s.
Return the cells to ice for 2–3 min.
Add 900 μL of SOC media to the DH10Bac competent cells.
Incubate at 37°C and 220 rpm for 4–5 h.
Plate the cells onto SOC agar containing 50 mg/mL kanamycin, 7 mg/mL gentamicin, 10 mg/mL tetracycline, 200 mg/mL Bluo-Gal, and 40 mg/mL IPTG.
Incubate at 37°C for 48–72 h under light protection by wrapping the plates in aluminum foil.
Use a single large white colony to inoculate 20 mL of SOC medium supplemented with 50 μg/mL kanamycin, 7 μg/mL gentamicin, and 10 μg/mL tetracycline.
Culture at 37°C and 220 rpm for 24 h.
Centrifuge the culture at 3,100 × g for 30 min.
Discard the supernatant and keep the cell pellet.
Collect the cell pellets in a 1.5 mL-microcentrifuge tube.
Perform bacmid extraction with a QIAGEN Plasmid Mini Kit in a laminar flow hood.
Add 300 μL of Buffer P1 to the tube containing cells and resuspend thoroughly.
Add 300 μL of Buffer P2 and gently invert the microcentrifuge tube 4–6 times for mixing.
Leave at room temperature until the solution fully changes color (approximately 5 min).
Add 300 μL of ice-cold Buffer P3 and mix by inverting the tube 4–6 times or until blue color disappears completely.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes after adding Buffer P3.
Centrifuge at 7,440 × g and 4°C for 10 min to pellet cellular debris.
Equilibrate the QIAGEN-tip by adding 5 volumes of Buffer QBT.
Allow the column to empty by gravity flow.
Transfer supernatant containing DNA onto an equilibrated QIAGEN-tip and allow it to flow through.
Wash the QIAGEN-tip twice with 2 mL of Buffer QC.
Elute bacmid DNA by adding 800 μL of Buffer QN to the QIAGEN-tip and allowing it to flow through.
Collect the eluate into a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 560 μL of sterile isopropanol into the tube containing eluted DNA.
Centrifuge at 7,440 × g and 4°C for 30 min.
Carefully decant the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold 70% ethanol.
Invert the tube gently several times to wash the DNA pellet.
Centrifuge at 7,440 × g and 4°C for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Air-dry the pellet for 15–20 min at room temperature.
Dissolve the DNA in 30 μL of TE buffer.
Store the purified recombinant bacmid at −20°C.
Culture Sf9 insect cells in Sf-900 II medium containing 50 units/mL penicillin and 50 μg/mL streptomycin.
Pipette Sf9 cells into a six-well plate so that each well contains up to 8 × 10^5 cells.
Add fresh antibiotic-free Sf-900 II medium to increase the total volume of the cell suspension to 2.5 mL per well.
Incubate at 27°C in the dark for 30 min to 1 h.
Change the medium to Grace’s Unsupplemented Insect Medium using a sterile pipette tip.
Take two sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 100 μL of Sf-900 II SFM medium to each tube.
Add 6 μL of transfection reagent to Tube 1.
Add 1 μg bacmid DNA to Tube 2.
Mix the contents within each tube.
Leave the tubes at room temperature for 30 min.
Transfer the contents of Tube 1 to Tube 2.
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Leave the mixture at room temperature for 30 min.
Add the bacmid: transfection reagent mixture to the cell in the well.
Mix gently by shaking the plate.
Incubate at 27°C for 5 h.
Replace the transfection mixture with fresh Sf-900 II medium.
Culture at 27°C for 4–5 days.
Aspirate the cell supernatant from the cells.
Transfer the aspirated supernatant to two 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes or a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 100 × g for 10 min to remove cell debris and collect supernatant containing clarified first-generation baculovirus (P1 virus) stock.
Prepare healthy Sf9 cells.
Add 8 × 10^6 cells to a T75 cell culture flask.
Add Sf-900 II medium to the final volume of 15 mL in the T75 cell culture flask.
Pre-warm the medium to 28°C in a thermostatic water bath.
Lay the culture flasks horizontally and place them at 28°C in the dark for more than 20 minutes.
After cells are attached to the surface of a T75 culture flask, add 0.4 mL of P1 virus stock to the flask.
Shake the flask gently to mix evenly.
Incubate at 28°C in the dark for 72 hours and monitor cell behavior under a microscope every other day.
After 72 hours, decant the medium into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 100 × g and 4°C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the clarified supernatant containing the high-titer P2 viral stock to a new centrifuge tube.
Store the P2 viral stock at −80°C to avoid repeated freezing and thawing.
Prepare 750 mL healthy Sf9 cells at 1.0–1.2 × 10^6 concentration in a cell culture flask.
Infect the prepared Sf9 cells with P3 virus stock at a volume ratio of 1:30.
Incubate infected cells at 27°C and 120 rpm for 72 h.
Centrifuge infected cells at 3,100 × g and 4°C for 15 min to harvest cells.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Collect the pelleted cells for storage or further processing.
Resuspend cell pellet in ice-cold Lysis buffer 2 by rocking or vortexing until fully dissolved.
Disrupt cells using sonication under specified conditions (two cycles, total cycle time 36 min, 150 W, 3 s pulse on, 8 s pulse off) while maintaining temperature control with a water-ice mixture.
Centrifuge cell lysate at 10,540 × g and 4°C for 30 min to remove debris and unbroken cells.
Collect the clarified supernatant from centrifugation.
Incubate clarified supernatant with Ni-NTA resin equilibrated in Lysis buffer 2 at 4°C for 1 h.
Rotate supernatant containing Ni-NTA mixture slowly and uniformly.
Transfer the mixture onto a column.
Allow supernatant to flow through the column.
Wash the column extensively with Lysis buffer 2.
Wash the column with Lysis buffer 2 containing 20 mM imidazole until no protein is detected in the eluate using Bradford reagent.
Equilibrate the column with 5 column volumes of Lysis buffer 2.
Leave 5 mL of buffer in the column and close it to prevent flow out.
Add 100 μL of PreScission Protease at a concentration of 1:100 (w/w) to beads.
Mix well and incubate for about 12 hours at 4°C.
Allow the enzyme digestion system to flow through the Ni-NTA column.
Wash the column extensively with Lysis buffer 2.
Elute Sr35 protein from the column using Lysis buffer 2 containing 20 mM imidazole.
Add PP protease directly to the Ni-NTA column bed to remove the SUMO tag.
Alternatively, remove the SUMO tag after eluting the target protein from the Ni-NTA column if necessary.
Analyze the eluate containing Sr35 on an SDS-PAGE gel for protein purity and quantity.
Select the Sr35 sample with better purity and higher quantity for further purification.
Purify the selected Sr35 sample through a GST affinity chromatography column to remove PP protease.
Pass the Sr35 sample through a GST column, collecting the eluate containing purified tagless Sr35.
Use a centrifugal filter (MWCO = 50 kDa) to pool the purified Sr35 and replace the buffer system with SEC buffer 2 (25 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 500 mM NaCl, 2 mM DTT).
Concentrate the purified Sr35 to the required volume for size exclusion chromatography (SEC).
Regularly measure protein concentration during the concentration process to prevent precipitation of Sr35 above 5 mg/mL.
Aliquot and dilute the Sr35 sample in sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes to achieve concentrations below 5 mg/mL in each tube.
Centrifuge at 7,440 × g and 4°C for 15 min.
Purify with size-exclusion chromatography using a Superdex 200 (10/300 GL) SEC column mounted.
Inject the prepared Sr35 sample via sample loop into the SEC column carefully to avoid disturbing precipitated protein.
Perform purification at a flow rate of 0.6 mL/min.
Collect fractions containing protein peaks and run SDS-PAGE analysis.
Pool and concentrate the fractions corresponding to pure and homogeneous Sr35 using a centrifugal filter (MWCO = 50 kDa).
Store concentrated and purified Sr35 at -80°C until further use.
Mix the purified AvrSr35ΔSP and Sr35 proteins to assemble the Sr35 resistosome in vitro.
Purify the complex with size-exclusion chromatography.
Mix purified Sr35 and AvrSr35∆SP at a ∼1:2 molar ratio.
Adjust the sodium chloride concentration of the mixture to 150 mM.
Add ATP to the final concentration of 1 mM.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 2 h.
Centrifuge the Sr35: AvrSr35ΔSP mixture at 7,440 × g and 4°C for 15 min.
Equilibrate a Superose 6 Increase 10/300GL column with SEC buffer 1.
Purify the mixture by injecting it into the size-exclusion chromatography column at a flow rate of 0.6 mL/min.
Collect fractions containing protein peaks.
Run SDS-PAGE analysis.
Select fractions corresponding to Sr35 resistosome for cryo-EM experiments.
Pool and concentrate the selected fractions to 0.5–3 mg/mL in SEC buffer using a centrifugal filter with MWCO of 100 kDa.
Dilute the Sr35 resistosome sample to 0.01–0.05 mg/mL.
Centrifuge the diluted sample at 4°C for 15 min.
Treat the grid with glow discharge (30–45 s at 15 mA).
Transfer 5 μL of sample supernatant onto a carbon-coated copper grid and let it stand for 1 min.
Absorb excess liquid from the grid with filter paper, ensuring not to completely blot the liquid.
Drop 4–6 μL of uranyl acetate onto the grid and absorb excess uranyl acetate three times.
Drop 4–6 μL of uranyl acetate onto the grid and let it stand for 1 min.
Absorb excess uranyl acetate with filter paper.
Observe the grid by transmission electron microscope.
Ultracentrifuge the Sr35 resistosome sample at 7,440 × g and 4°C for 10 min in a Micro-Ultracentrifuge.
Transfer the supernatant into sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Dilute the Sr35 resistosome sample to five gradient concentrations: 3 mg/mL, 2.5 mg/mL, 2 mg/mL, 1.5 mg/mL, 1 mg/mL, and 0.5 mg/mL.
Pipette 5 μL of each protein solution onto a separate freshly glow-discharged grid (QuantiFoil-1.2/1.3-Cu 300 mesh holey carbon grid).
Absorb excess solution from the grid with 3–6 s of blotting at 100% humidity and 4°C before plunging the grids into liquid ethane.
Transfer the grid into a pre-cooled sample box.
Keep in liquid nitrogen until further experiments.
Acquire data using EPU software to control the 300 kV transmission electron microscope operated at a nominal magnification of 105,000× with a pixel size of 1.095 Å.
Record pre-screening specimen images with a defocus range of -1.2 to -1.8 μm in super-resolution mode with 32 frames per movie and a total dose of 50 electrons per Å².
Align, dose-weight, and sum the 32 frames of each movie using MotionCor2, resulting in summed micrographs at a pixel size of 1.095 Å per pixel.
Import the micrographs with dose-weighting into Relion software and estimate contrast transfer function (CTF) parameters by running CTFFIND-4.1.
Select micrographs with visible Thon rings at better than 4 Å resolution.
Perform particles auto-picking by Laplacian-of-Gaussian filter with a diameter for LoG filter set to 200–250 Å.
Extract ∼20,000 particles from the first autopick with ‘‘Particle box size’’ set to 400 and ‘‘Rescaled size’’ set to 100.
Perform two-dimensional (2D) class averaging with ‘‘Number of classes’’ set to 200 and ‘‘mask diameter’’ set to 340 Å to generate templates for further template-based auto picking.
Select any orientation particle images from 2D classification to generate template images.
Perform a template-based auto picking using the generated templates.
Extract particles as in step e for further 2D classification.
After two rounds of reference-2D classification, select ∼150,000 particles from well-defined particle images.
Use selected particles for generation of the initial 3D model.
Subject particles to 3D classification into 4 classes according to C1 symmetry.
Select the best class corresponding to the Sr35 resistosome decamer.
Extract particles for the best 3D class without binning to the original pixel size (1.095 Å/pixel).
Select the optimal classification with 35,510 particles for the final 3D auto-refinement with imposed symmetry C5.
Perform post-processing of the map to achieve a resolution of 3.3 Å (FSC = 0.143).
Create five local masks corresponding to different coordinates in local maps for particle subtraction.
Carry out particle subtraction in 3D classification without performing image alignment.
Perform two rounds of 3D classification.
Carry out 3D auto-refinement of an optimal local electron density map.
Use the processed electron density map with a resolution of 3.6 Å (FSC = 0.143) for further analysis.
Model build and refine Sr35 resistosome induced by AvrSr35ΔSP_R381A at a 3.3 Å resolution.
Perform initial model building in the SWISS-MODEL server using the structure of ZAR1 resistosome (PDB ID: 6J5T) as a template.
Dock the structure of the ZAR1 resistosome into the EM density of Sr35 resistosome in Chimera.
Dock five ATP molecules into the density using COOT.
Refine the model of five ATP-bound Sr35-AvrSr35 molecules in PHENIX based on the EM map in real space with secondary structure and geometric constraints.
Verify the structural model using MolProbity included in the PHENIX package.
